leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single-part B014 prize on GLP-1 physiology and incretin therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity. Five members (El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson) name Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, with a citation covering both the physiology and its translation into long-acting therapies. Wahren-Herlenius names Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, with a discovery-side citation on the physiology of GLP-1 and its active forms, and states that her configuration is the wrong one if the committee decides the drug-development step must be recognised. Shared: Drucker and Holst, the stable mechanism, and independent outcome trials. Not shared: whether the third name is Knudsen or Mojsov, and whether the citation is discovery-only or discovery plus drug design. Svenningsson says in a response that he would accept Mojsov in place of Knudsen if the committee prefers a discovery-only citation, provided the reasoning is stated explicitly.

areas_of_agreement: All six members explicitly prefer a single-part B014 prize, and each says the case rests on the science and not on the unanimity of the opening ballots.
Drucker and Holst appear in all six configurations; no member proposes a GLP-1 prize without them.

The GLP-1 mechanism is described as stable and replicated, with large independent randomised outcome trials in type 2 diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular and renal disease; no member raises a maturity objection to the core claim.

All six name B006 (CAR-T) as an alternative. Four (El-Manira, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson) also name B008 (optogenetics), Linnarsson names B016 (SMN2 antisense) and Wahren-Herlenius names B031 (cGAS-STING). These are stated alternatives, not counted as preferred configurations.

All six state that the three-person limit forces the exclusion of at least one credible name on B014, and that the priority record on early GLP-1 work (Mojsov, and Habener outside the supplied credit list) cannot be settled from the supplied evidence.
scientific_disputes: Whether the prize should honour GLP-1 discovery alone or discovery together with the medicinal chemistry that produced long-acting analogues. Five members include Knudsen's acylated analogues as part of what the discovery became; Wahren-Herlenius treats the discovery side as the Nobel tradition and notes that her trio stops short of the clinical achievement.

Whether industrial drug design belongs in a Physiology or Medicine citation at all. El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg and Svenningsson each raise it as a reservation against their own configuration; Sandberg says some colleagues may reject it.

Whether optogenetics (B008), described by El-Manira as a causal method with exceptional originality but mainly a research tool with clinical use still emerging, should rank above or below a clinical therapy candidate such as CAR-T (B006).
Whether Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer is the same achievement as CAR design (raised by Wahren-Herlenius), which bears on how a CAR-T citation would be worded.
attribution_disputes: Third place on B014: Knudsen (five members) or Mojsov (Wahren-Herlenius). Members record Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active truncated peptide as a credible claim whose priority is contested.

Habener is outside the supplied credit list but is described by El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg and Svenningsson as part of the same priority discussion. Svenningsson argues that a contested edge is not a contested core, because Holst and Drucker are secure under any reading; this has not been tested against the other members.

Optogenetics (B008) has six credited names. El-Manira proposes Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel; Svenningsson asks whether excluding Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck can be defended. No member has put forward an alternative split.

CAR-T (B006): Linnarsson, Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius question the absence of Eshhar from the credited names, and Linnarsson notes it may force the citation to be worded around costimulated, clinically validated CARs.
SMN2 antisense (B016) is described by Linnarsson as the cleanest attribution on the shortlist (Krainer and Bennett), though he regards it as a single therapeutic story with narrower impact.
maturity_disputes: Long-term safety and effects beyond weight and glycaemia for the incretin class are still accumulating. El-Manira, Linnarsson, Sandberg and Svenningsson say they cannot verify the latest outcome data from the supplied materials; none treats this as disqualifying.
Optogenetics: El-Manira notes clinical use is still emerging, so maturity depends on whether a research method is weighed on the same footing as a validated therapy.
No member argues that B014 is premature; maturity is raised as a framing issue for B014 and a weighting issue for B008.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson (chair) discloses about twenty co-authored works with Perlmann on topics unrelated to the shortlist, and training with Paul Greengard, who is not a candidate. He does not regard either as requiring recusal.
Perlmann discloses ties to Ronald Evans and Johan Ericson and co-authorship with Svenningsson and El-Manira; none concerns the shortlisted candidates.
El-Manira discloses a 2009 co-authored paper with Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons and shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation; no recusal is apparent.

Linnarsson discloses eight co-authored works with Sandberg and the 2016 spatial transcriptomics paper; Sandberg discloses single-cell co-authorship with Linnarsson and Frisen. None of the shortlisted ballots concerns that work.

Wahren-Herlenius notes that her field (autoimmunity) is near cGAS-STING and CAR-T in autoimmune applications, with no documented connection to any credited candidate, and does not infer one from shared topics or affiliations.
No member reports a specific conflict with any credited candidate on any shortlisted ballot, and no recusal is requested in the six files.
questions_for_round2: Should the B014 citation honour GLP-1 discovery alone (Drucker, Holst, Mojsov) or discovery plus long-acting drug design (Drucker, Holst, Knudsen)? What explicit reasoning would the committee record for either choice?

Can the committee state a defensible basis for placing Mojsov or Knudsen third, given that Mojsov's priority on the active peptide is contested and Knudsen's contribution is industrial drug design? How should Habener's absence from the supplied credit list be handled?

Is a single-topic B014 prize preferable to pairing it with a second distinct achievement such as B006, given the three-person cap and the exclusions a pairing would force? Raised by El-Manira and Sandberg.

If a second part is considered, which of B006, B008, B016 or B031 is the strongest, and what laureate split holds up for it? Specifically: can B008 be split among six credited names without excluding Bamberg, and can B006 be defended without Eshhar?
How much weight should unresolved long-term safety data on incretin therapies carry in the wording of the B014 citation, and does any member see it as affecting timing?
summary.chair_observation: The six round-1 files agree on B014 as the single preferred prize and diverge only on its third laureate and on whether the citation is discovery-only or discovery plus translation. Five of six name Knudsen and one names Mojsov, and Svenningsson says he could accept the other configuration if the reasoning is stated. Round 1 does not yet show which second achievement, if any, the committee would pair with B014; every member lists B006 as an alternative but none has proposed a laureate split for a second part. These are counts of explicit positions in the six files only.
